title: Bitcoin Has Fallen 50% From Its Peak. History Points to What Comes Next.
author: Anders Bylund
description: Bitcoin has declined 50% from its October 2025 peak of $126,128, following the established halving cycle pattern. Historical data suggests recovery could take 2-3 years, with the next halving in April 2028 potentially catalyzing the next bull cycle. The cryptocurrency is increasingly acting like a traditional asset due to institutional adoption via spot Bitcoin ETFs (launched January 2024), improved regulatory clarity, and miners diversifying into AI computing contracts.

Mentioned alongside Mara Holdings as a major miner leveraging AI computing contracts to stabilize revenue during periods of reduced mining profitability.

title: How TeraWulf’s Anthropic Deal Booted Up a $19B AI Empire
author: Jeffrey Neal Johnson
description: TeraWulf Inc. secured a landmark 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic worth an estimated $19 billion, transitioning from volatile cryptocurrency mining to stable, high-margin AI infrastructure hosting. The company sold its stake in the Abernathy Joint Venture for $450 million to fund the 401-megawatt Justified Data campus in Kentucky. This shift from unpredictable mining rewards (~$87,000/MW/month) to utility-grade AI workloads (~$149,000/MW/month) fundamentally improves margins and revenue visibility, while high institutional ownership and elevated short interest create potential for significant price appreciation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Secured a transformative $19B contract with Anthropic, transitioning to higher-margin AI workloads, improved revenue predictability, strong institutional backing (62.49% ownership), and strategic capital recycling through asset sales to fund growth without dilution.
Mentioned as a peer attempting similar mining-to-AI infrastructure transitions, but without specific details about their progress or success relative to TeraWulf.

title: Why TeraWulf, IREN, and Other Data Center Stocks Jumped Today
author: Joe Tenebruso
description: TeraWulf surged after securing a blockbuster 20-year, $19 billion deal with AI company Anthropic for 401 megawatts of computing capacity at its Kentucky data center. IREN also jumped on reports it could secure a similar lucrative agreement with Anthropic for up to 1.4 gigawatts of Australian data center capacity valued at $15 billion. Both stocks benefited from strong demand for AI infrastructure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Secured a major 20-year, $19 billion contract with Anthropic for 401 megawatts of computing capacity, validating its strategy and providing long-duration revenue streams. Stock rose 4.84%.

Positioned as a leading candidate for Anthropic's Australian data center project valued up to $15 billion. Analyst upgraded stock to buy with $58 price target and projects revenue growth from $717 million to $8.5 billion by 2028. Stock rose 12.89%.

title: Here's Why Bloom Energy Stock Rallied Again Today
author: Howard Smith
description: Bloom Energy stock surged 9.3% as of midday trading, driven by continued momentum in AI infrastructure demand. The rally was fueled by Anthropic's announcement of a $19 billion data center lease with TeraWulf, following Bloom's expanded $25 billion partnership with Brookfield last week. Bloom's solid-oxide fuel cell technology is becoming critical for powering AI data centers, with the stock up over 240% year-to-date.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock rallied 9.3% on strong demand signals from AI sector announcements. Expanded $25 billion partnership with Brookfield and growing recognition as key solution for AI data center power needs. Up 240% year-to-date, though article notes lofty valuation makes it speculative.
